career_ladder.note: Field executive hierarchy within the Maharashtra Forest Department (वन विभाग, महाराष्ट्र शासन). Forest Guards (Vanrakshak) are responsible for beat patrolling, wildlife protection, prevention of timber smuggling, anti-poaching operations, and forest fire control across territorial circles and tiger reserves (Tadoba-Andhari, Melghat, Pench, Sahyadri, Navegaon-Nagzira). Promotion to Forester and Range Forest Officer is regulated under Maharashtra Forest Subordinate Service Rules based on seniority-cum-merit and departmental qualifying tests.

exam_scheme.note: Selection is conducted in two stages carrying a combined total of 200 marks. Stage 1 is an online Computer Based Test (CBT) of 60 questions carrying 120 marks (2 marks per question) over 120 minutes conducted by TCS iON. Candidates scoring a minimum of 45% marks (54/120) in the CBT qualify for the Stage 2 Physical Efficiency Test carrying 80 marks. There is no negative marking in the CBT. Final selection is strictly based on aggregate marks in CBT (120) and Physical Test (80).

financial_package.note: Forest Guards in the Government of Maharashtra Forest Department are remunerated under Maharashtra Civil Services (Revised Pay) Rules, 2019, strictly separate from Central 7th CPC structures.
financial_package.pay_source_label: Maharashtra Civil Services (Revised Pay) Rules, 2019, Schedule (Forest Guard Scale S-7)
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated on Level S-7 entry basic pay of ₹21,700 with 58% DA (₹12,586 effective 01.07.2025), HRA (9% to 27% depending on posting circle: ₹1,953 in forest field postings to ₹5,859 in urban division headquarters), Forest Duty Allowance / Naxal Area Special Allowance (for Gadchiroli/Chandrapur divisions), net of NPS/DCPS deduction (10% of Basic + DA = ₹3,429) and profession tax (₹200).
